description:
**Problem**
Crash consistency and origin_seq uniqueness must hold across the append/fsync/index/apply/receipt pipeline (REALTIME_PLAN.md §6.5). There is no model that explores crash cut points and recovery behavior.

**Design Notes**
This is an abstract model of ordering, not a full WAL implementation.
design:
**Design**
Create a Stateright model that encodes the durability ordering from Plan §6.5: allocate seq, write record, fsync, index commit, apply, receipt finalize, reply. Allow a crash at each cut point and a recovery step that replays durable records and reconciles PENDING receipts (Plan §0.11).

Properties: no origin_seq reuse after recovery, LocalFsync receipts imply event survives crash, and recovery finds durable-but-unindexed events (todo.md Model #8).

Keep the state small (counters + flags) but align the cut points to the plan language.
title: Stateright: WAL crash recovery cut points

acceptance_criteria:
**Acceptance**
- [ ] Planner marks a TTL bead referenced by live `core` work as pinned and not eligible.
- [ ] Planner does not pin a TTL bead merely because it points outward to durable work.
- [ ] Planner handles same-namespace TTL refs deterministically without order-dependent results.
- [ ] Skip reason includes enough data for admin output to explain the pinning ref.
- [ ] Tests include cross-namespace and same-namespace pinning cases.
description:
**Problem**
TTL namespaces can hold sidecar or wisp beads that durable workflow beads reference. Sweeping those sidecars while durable incoming refs still exist would make graph traversal and human context brittle.

**Files**
- GC planner module from the previous bead
- `crates/beads-core` graph/ref helpers only if an existing helper cannot answer incoming refs cleanly
design:
**Design**
Extend the pure GC planner with conservative incoming-reference pinning.

A candidate bead in a TTL namespace is pinned if it has any incoming live reference from another live bead whose namespace is `Forever` or whose source bead is not currently GC-eligible in the same planning pass. Outgoing references from the TTL bead do not pin it.

Start conservative: any incoming live edge pins, regardless of dependency kind. If edge-kind relaxation is needed later, file it separately.

notes.author: darin@darinsmcstudio2.lan
notes.content: Prediscovery: incoming reference queries should use StoreState::deps_to(&BeadRef) from crates/beads-core/src/namespaced_state.rs; do not scan only the local CanonicalState because cross-namespace edges live in the owning child namespace. Parent edges are DepKind::Parent and ordinary deps share DepKey, so conservative first pass can treat all incoming live DepKey values as pins. Liveness check should use StoreState::resolve_ref(key.from_ref()).is_some() and skip tombstoned sources.

title: Add conservative incoming-reference pinning to GC planning
